angle: WR/TE break mechanics: one metric (Break G, average g over the second around the first cut: braking in, turning, driving out), graded by the same code on Combine route drills and sampled NFL snaps of the same route family (slant/out/hitch/in/corner), tested against full-season NGS separation over expected on held-out draft classes. Revision of round 24 cand_2 (7.78).
metric_name: Break G (how hard a receiver plants: average g over the one second around his first real cut; z-scored within drill and Combine year, averaged over drills, shrunk for few drills)
headline_number: -1.2 in of career SOE per sd of drill Break G [90%: -3.7, +1.0], n=116, each class scored by a forecast fit on the other two (pick + 40 + weight + NGS + TE). Per-class held-out slopes 2023 -1.1, 2024 -1.9, 2025 -0.3. Team-clustered interval -4.0 to +1.2 (32 teams); one-sided placebo p=0.81. Drill-to-NFL Break G rho -0.05 (n=101) vs official 40 to NFL top speed 0.46 (n=100). Clubs pay 14% earlier pick per sd for it.
what_changed_from_previous: Fixes the three round-24 fatal flaws. (1) x-y route paths: new hero Fig 1 draws 35 rotated route paths per family, drill vs NFL, coloured by speed, above the speed-through-plant traces; new Fig 4 overlays each named receiver's own drill cuts on his own NFL breaks of the same family. (2) No null forest plots left: transfer is now a one-dot-per-receiver scatter pair (40 vs top speed, drill vs NFL Break G); the held-out test is a residual scatter with one fitted line per held-out class, the +/-3 in margin as a wedge and the placebo histogram beside it; the same-snap section is text only; player cards dropped. (3) Filenames now match caption numbers (fig1..fig4). Data science: team-clustered bootstrap (32 teams), one-sided placebo p and one-sided R2-gain p, per-class held-out slopes (class interaction), and a max-statistic shuffle correction across the 30 drill-to-NFL cells (braking 0.12 lead gives adjusted p 1.00, now stated as not a finding). Football: Table 2 expanded to 5 named receivers (Boutte, Smith, Nacua, Flournoy, Bobo) with class, pick, routes, a tracking-located clip and its official play-log result, plus a verdict column; Monday section adds a scout bullet and the expected 2026 count. Writeup: lede caveat (one pre-set metric, bounded null), football 'why now', each lede number once. 1,991 words, 4 figures + 2 tables.
open_risks: Still a null-result paper; the re-stem prescription and the 'do not pay for cut grade' rule are untested proposals.
Table 2 verdicts come from tracking and the play log; nobody has watched the clips, so film verification is not met.
Section 4 (same-snap) is descriptive and its before/after-throw split was chosen after a first look; the timing placebo fails (-13.5).
Not blind: all three classes were seen in earlier rounds; team bootstrap, placebos, class slopes and Section 4 were added after the main test was frozen.
Fig 1 path panels show 35 randomly sampled reps per cell; drill entry speed is only marginally faster than NFL on slants (4.3 vs 4.1 yd/s).
Game tracking is a 40-play sample per player, half top-EPA, with no defenders or ball; analysis.py takes about 100 s.
Angle has plateaued around 8.2-8.5 across many rounds; the winner (DL Hoop G) is likely to stay ahead.
